Findings.Comment: The mutex is locked at the start but remains locked when the team slug is not found. The error path returns without unlocking, which will cause a deadlock on any subsequent call that attempts to lock the mutex.
Findings.Headline: Mutex unlock missing on error path — deadlock

When `r.Ticket` is nil, this line will trigger a nil pointer dereference and crash the program. The fix is to restore the early return or adjust the logic to handle nil tickets.
Findings.Headline: Nil pointer dereference when Ticket is nil — blocking

Findings.Comment: The change modifies the bounds check in `ContextAfter` from `last > len(lines)` to `last >= len(lines)`, which correctly catches the edge case where `last` equals the slice length. However, setting `last = len(lines) + 1` creates an out-of-bounds index. When `first` is less than `last` (e.g., a hunk near the end of the file requesting context), the subsequent slice `lines[first:last]` will panic because the upper bound exceeds the slice length by one. For example, with a 10-line file, a hunk at line 8, and n=2, `first` becomes 10 and `last` becomes 11, causing a runtime panic on the return statement.
Findings.Headline: ContextAfter bounds logic will panic on slice out-of-bounds

Expected.why: The clamp sets last to len(lines)+1, so the final slice expression lines[first:last] runs one past the length. With no spare capacity that panics; with spare capacity it silently yields a phantom trailing line, which is the quieter half of the bug.
The response body is never closed on any path, so the underlying connection is leaked on every call, successful or not.
The worker goroutine writes q.depth and reads q.pending without holding q.mu, while Submit writes and Depth reads the same fields under the mutex; that is a data race.
